So I have been in IT since I was 19, I got into the field because I wanted something challenging and with good career options in the future, I also love technology and building systems.

I am now 27 and while I still love tech and building systems I want to get out for the following reasons:

  • Working in an office sucks ! its bad for your health, you don't get to use your hands and you get fat from a lack of activity, which I then have to spend an extra hour a day at gym to keep off.

  • Once you get past 40 job certainty is scary, I see a lot of guys past 40 or older get a tap on the shoulder and replaced with someone cheaper, even the exceptional ones have this issue I have a mate in his late 50's working for a multinational software company in a very senior role yet even he admits her never knows when his career will come to an end, that rarely happens to tradespeople.

  • Corporate events and parties are mandatory, going out to events is torture when you are being forced to do it, I have never minded overtime when it is actual work however spending 4 hours on a Tuesday night schmoozing some government employee is hell, not to mention the effect it has on your health.

  • I don't want to be 50 and working in an office, self explanatory.

So the idea of becoming an electrician interests me, I discovered that a 1st year apprentice electrician thanks to the Australian governments mature age apprentice subsidy makes around 5% less than I do per week, I have a lot of skill Phone Systems, Data cabling and IT with the corresponding certifications to match, which after speaking to a few small electricians said would be desirable for commercial work.

So, thoughts ?

If you were me where would you get started ?
So into my late 20's I am looking at a career change from IT to Electrical, anyone in electrical or similar got any tips ?

I did a little bit, very little, during two summers while I was in school and this was a long time ago. You had not received any replies so I will offer what I can think of. It is not much but it may help.

Be certain you want to change. It may suck to have your job but you have a job. Getting an education, specifically for electrical workers, while gainfully employed elsewhere, may be an option. That whole adage about a bird in the hand and grass being greener (I'm not so good at adages) has a point. It may be valid along with that whole look before you leap adage.

Most importantly, and this is from personal experience, do your best to be employed with a company that does new construction only. Be it plumbing, electricity, rehabilitation, or even hanging cabinets - working on existing structures sucks in so many ways when compared with working on new construction. When I designed my current home, I did so with the idea that it has to last me the rest of my life. Things are as exposed as they can be and my walls are full of conduit. My garage is large and has half of it is a wood shop - I designed that so that it even has a raceway across both sides. I wish I had done bus lines in the house but there are electrical and communications conduits throughout and a drop of each to all four walls in every room where it is practical.

As an envelope house, it is easier than some and I've not had to do any major work on it yet. Future proofing is not something that I think most home owners or building contractors gave much of a thought to. Working on existing structures is not a very fun thing to do. It's dirty, cramped, and generally more work than it is worth.

Also, I would look into the health aspects. You're in your late 20s so you have plenty of hit points left. I'd be curious as to the health of those tradesmen when compared to office workers and I'd want to refine that information to include those (of both sets) who are actively trying to maintain their health. You probably will find that there's less wear and tear on your body in an office and that the chances of a traumatic injury are much lower for office workers than they are for electricians. If health is your goal then you may be better suited in an office environment than you are in the electrical field.

Well... That concludes the entirety of what I would say that I know about the subject that would have some potential value to you. I knew a guy, an old fellow, who has since passed on but he had built houses (including all the various trades that go into them - kind of a jack of all trades and self-employed) and he was fond of a saying and he used it often. He built my pole barn but that's another story. His colloquialism was this: "Black to black, white to white, and shit don't flow uphill." Needless to say, I had the lighting/electricity installed by a professional but he was an interesting character.

Edit: Added "two" because I wanted to ensure that it was clear that I was not to be confused with an electrician. I was not a journeyman or anything fancy. I snaked a bunch of wire, hung lights, installed switches and outlets, and then still had to leave the boxes open to be inspected by a qualified professional before being closed and the power turned on. Your local regulations may well be different than they were back in Massachusetts at the time. It was a college summer job. I never electrocuted myself nor burned anything down so I guess I did okay.
